overview: Rise 5.99's NoFall is the largest module in the batch: a ModeSetting with fourteen registered modes, thirteen live switch cases, and the "Artemis" entry registered but absent from the switch, which makes selecting it a no-op. Every mode runs from onPreMotion and shares two gates: the handler returns early while the HighJump module is enabled, and every mode requires PlayerUtil.isBlockUnder() to succeed, so none of the techniques fire over open air or in the void. A hand-rolled fallDist accumulator sums the per-tick delta of the client's fallDistance instead of reading the field directly. The modes split into three families: event ground-flag spoofs (Ground Spoof, Tick, Artemis 2, Math Ground, Less Fall, Verus, Hypixel), explicit packet sends (Packet, Collision Silent, Vulcan), and movement-state manipulation (Collision, No Ground, Matrix).

sections.p: onPreMotion fires once per tick before the C03 is built. offGroundTicks counts consecutive off-ground ticks, reset on any grounded tick, and fallDist accumulates fallDistance minus the previous tick's value, reset whenever the field reads zero, which makes the accumulator track sustained fall rather than instantaneous distance. The HighJump gate and the isBlockUnder gate run before the switch and apply to every mode, including Matrix. The dispatch is a string compare on the ModeSetting, and because "Artemis" has no matching case, that selection falls through the whole switch silently.

The event-flag family claims ground on the PreMotionEvent, which the client folds into the next C03. Ground Spoof and Tick fire on accumulated fallDist > 2, with Tick adding a ticksExisted % 3 cadence; Math Ground and Less Fall require posY to sit within 0.005 of the 1/64 grid before claiming; Verus bounds the claim to fallDist between 3 and 12 with the same grid alignment; Artemis 2 claims every 8 ticks at fallDist > 2; Hypixel waits until ticksExisted > 150 and then claims when fallDistance minus a tick-scaled offset stays non-negative, incrementing the tick counter each claim. The packet family sends its own C03s: Packet emits a bare C03PacketPlayer(true) at fallDist > 2, Collision Silent sends a full C06PacketPlayerPosLook whose y is snapped to the 1/64 grid with onGround true, and Vulcan snaps the position to the 0.015625 grid, clamps motionY to -0.4, sends C03(true) and drops the timer to 0.9 for that tick.

The grid-snapped modes (Math Ground, Less Fall, Verus, Collision Silent, Vulcan) align the claimed y to the sub-pixel grid that landing heuristics expect, so the onGround claim sits on a coordinate that looks like a block boundary even though the player is airborne. Collision sets motionY to -(posY - posY % 1/64), pulling the player onto the grid line while claiming ground, and Matrix goes the opposite way: it forces onGround false permanently, runs strafe and jump logic, and manipulates motionX/motionZ so the player never appears grounded. No Ground also forces onGround false and optionally jitters the event y by 0.0001-0.001 on grounded ticks. The packet-mode emits are extra C03s beyond the one-per-tick movement stream, raising the server-observed packet rate whenever a send mode is active.

files.label: NoFall.java
files.explanation: The full module: fourteen registered modes, the dead "Artemis" selection, the fallDist accumulator, the offGroundTicks counter, and the HighJump plus isBlockUnder gates. The switch shows all three families, from the plain event-flag claims through the grid-snapped Verus and Math Ground modes to the explicit C03 and C06PacketPlayerPosLook sends and the motion-level Matrix and No Ground manipulation. The Vulcan branch additionally rewrites mc.timer.timerSpeed, coupling a timer change into the spoof.

files.label: PlayerUtil.java (isBlockUnder gate)
files.explanation: The terrain predicate every NoFall mode depends on. isBlockUnder() sweeps a copy of the player's bounding box downward from posY plus eye height in 2-block steps, returning true on the first collision, with an overload that applies an x/z offset to the sweep box. Because the NoFall handler returns before the switch when this returns false, the entire module is inert over open air and in the void, which is a deliberate safety property of the client's design: NoFall only operates when there is terrain to land on.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (block-cache ground truth)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly never trusts the C03 onGround bit. In check() the from and to ground states come from RichBoundsLocation.isOnGround() (lines 138-140), a block-cache scan at minY minus the yOnGround epsilon, optionally widened through isOnGroundOpportune against the BlockChangeTracker; the packet flag plays no part. The vertical allowance comes from vDistRel, which seeds the allowed distance from the previous move's momentum and only accepts a handful of named envelopes (zero-y move on ground, jump, step-up, riptide launch), and the violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 with a set-back to the stored location.

Rise's flag-only C03 from the Packet mode and the event-flag rides from the flag family arrive with the player over air whenever the grid-snap fails to coincide with a real block. NCP's block-cache ground state contradicts the claim, so the descent is scored against the vDistRel fall envelope; the 1/64 grid-snapped positions shift y by less than 0.015625, which is sub-0.03 and ignored for movement purposes, so the snap does not rescue the claim. The claim is simply ignored: SurvivalFly keeps enforcing the fall envelope against the ray-traced ground state, so a ground spoof buys no leniency in the vertical model and the client-side fallDistance reset is invisible to NCP because the server tracks its own heights. The companion check moving/player/NoFall.java keeps its own noFallMaxY / noFallFallDistance bookkeeping and deals the fall damage itself through handleOnGround, so zeroing the client field never cancels the damage NCP has already accounted.

countering.label: NoFall (ground-location cross-check)
countering.explanation:
Vrekt's NoFall compares three independently derived states. MovingListener computes ground from the world (LocationHelper.isOnGround) and stores the location as groundLocation whenever it is grounded; PacketListener records the raw packet flag into MovingData via setFlyingClientOnGround(flying.getOnGround()); and Bukkit tracks the server-side fall distance. NoFall.check() fires when the vertical distance from the last grounded location is at least 3.0 blocks, the player is descending, Vrekt's own ground state says airborne, the client claimed onGround, and the server fall distance is exactly 0.0, producing the violation "Fall distance is 0 while not onGround. (Client faked)" and player.damage(toGround) on cancel.

Every claim zeroes the server-side fall distance through vanilla onGround handling, whichever family produced it. The first descent past 3.0 blocks below the last grounded location, with Vrekt's own ground state airborne and the server fall distance at zero, trips the faked-ground violation; the grid-aligned y positions do not change the check's own ground calculation, which uses LocationHelper against the world, not the packet's coordinate. The 3.0-block descent requirement is the tolerance: genuine short hops and real landings pass. The bypass is to claim ground only when the position truly touches a block, which is exactly the behavior the module exists to fake.

countering.label: GroundSpoof (predicted-position trace)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's GroundSpoof derives its own ground state on every MoveEvent. For position updates it reads event.isOnGroundReally(), which is already lag-compensated; for flag-only updates it runs AdjacentBlocks.onGroundReally on the predicted position with the predicted velocity Y at a 0.001 tolerance. When the event claims onGround but the trace reports air, the check re-tests the pre-move position with the Y already clipped (mirroring the client's clip-then-flag order), skips steps and web-phasing cases, and otherwise punishes with a rubber-band. With the preventNoFall setting enabled, setNotOnGround rewrites the raw packet bytes so the onGround flag is forced to false on the wire, actively undoing the spoof before the server processes it.

Hawk checks the claim against its own lag-compensated trace for both flag-only and position updates, so the grid-snapped C06 from Collision Silent and the bare C03 from Packet are handled the same way: onGroundReally reports air, the pre-move re-test at the clipped Y also fails, and the check punishes with a rubber-band and, with preventNoFall on, rewrites the packet's onGround byte to false. The step exemption covers only real step-up moves, which a falling player is not performing. The 0.001-0.02 tolerances and the lag-compensated position mean threshold-timed claims over air are caught as soon as the trace disagrees, and the flag rewrite neutralizes the payload even when the server would otherwise accept it.

countering.label: NoFall (post-prediction collision check)
countering.explanation:
Grim's NoFall runs as a PacketReceiveListener on PLAYER_FLYING and PLAYER_ROTATION after the prediction engine has already simulated the tick. For any packet that claims onGround true and carries no position change (wrapper.isOnGround() && !wrapper.hasPositionChanged()), it builds a 0.6 by 0.001 feet box at the simulated x, y, z, expands it by the player's movement threshold, and collides it against the compensated world plus nearby hard entities. If nothing is under the player it flags with the 10-tick setback from the check data and, when packet modification is allowed, rewrites the onGround bit to false and re-encodes the packet.

The Packet mode's bare C03(true) is a flag-only PLAYER_FLYING packet, the exact case Grim's post-prediction NoFall handles: no collision under the simulated feet box, flag with the 10-tick setback, rewrite the bit. The position-bearing spoofs (Collision Silent C06, Vulcan's snapped C03, and all event-flag rides on full movement packets) are deliberately skipped by this check and land in the prediction-based GroundSpoof domain, which compares the whole simulated move against the compensated world. The position-less onGround claim is the exact wire shape the check targets; position-bearing spoofs fall to the prediction-based GroundSpoof check instead, since this one deliberately skips packets that changed position.
